# Implementation layers

The smallest useful proof is **one versioned unusual problem, one consented answer, an anchored human score, and an evidence-linked feedback report**. It tests whether a first-session answer can expose creativity, analysis and ingenuity in an inspectable way. No predictive claim follows from that proof.

| Layer | Added capability | Evidence before adding the next layer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L0 meaning | Define Pack, role/construct map, one case and rubric, synthetic answers. | Expert review finds the case answerable and scoring anchors interpretable. |
| L1 human challenge | Local recording or accessible alternate mode, consent, manual transcription/correction, blind human ratings, feedback. | Participants understand purpose; recording, rights and rating journey work. |
| L2 controlled AI | ASR and AI evidence extraction with pinned versions, human calibration and replay. | AI errors and uncertainty are measurable and correctable. |
| L3 three-session challenge | Technical and cooperation cases, bank rotation, generator review, score report and exposure controls. | Cross-case/rater stability and accessible completion. |
| L4 research platform | Cohort assignment, blinded outcomes, experiment registry, subgroup/error analysis and deletion lineage. | Prospective study can be audited without selection use. |
| L5 decision aid | Named role/employer policy, accepted validation, human review, appeal and monitoring. | Actual owner/legal decisions and ongoing evidence. |

Do not build employer ranking into L0-L3. The expensive irreversible boundary is participant data and employment impact, so rights and provenance appear early. Features such as elaborate proctoring, adaptive difficulty and automatic pass/fail have no place in the minimum proof without demonstrated need and separate validation.
